# Configuration reference

Scan options can live in your project instead of on the command line. TODO Notifier reads `[tool.todonotifier]` from `pyproject.toml`, or a
`.todonotifier.toml` file with the same keys at the top level (drop the `tool.todonotifier` prefix from the table names). `todonotifier init` writes a
commented starter file.

**Discovery.** Starting at the scan path (its directory, if it is a file), TODO Notifier walks up to the git root (or the filesystem root). In each
directory `.todonotifier.toml` is checked first, then `pyproject.toml` (only if it has a `[tool.todonotifier]` table). The first file found wins, and
`--config PATH` overrides discovery. With no file, the defaults apply. When files are named on the command line (as pre-commit does) and all of them are
inside the current directory, discovery starts at the current directory.

**Precedence**, highest first: command line flags, the config file, the command line and config file defaults (the "CLI default" column below), then
the `ScanSettings` defaults (the "library default" column), which only the Python API uses.

Unknown keys and wrong types fail with a message that names the key and the file, for example
`Unknown key 'tagz' in pyproject.toml [tool.todonotifier]. Did you mean 'tags'?` (exit code 2).

```toml
# .todonotifier.toml (in pyproject.toml, put these under [tool.todonotifier])
tags = ["TODO", "FIXME"]
default_due_days = 60
fail_on = "expired"

[exclude_dirs]
name = ["generated", "vendor"]

[authors]
"ashu@example.com" = "ashu"

[notify.slack]
webhook_env = "TODO_SLACK_WEBHOOK"
```

## Scan options

The "CLI default" is what `todonotifier` and the config file use when a key is not set; "same" means it equals the library default. The library default is what `ScanSettings()` (the Python API) uses.

| Key | Type | Library default | CLI default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `paths` | `list[str]` | `["."]` | same | Directories and/or individual files to scan. In a config file, relative paths are relative to the directory of the file. |
| `extensions` | `list[str]` | `["py"]` | `"common"` | File extensions to scan, without the leading dot (a leading dot is stripped). In the config file this can also be a string. The name `"common"` expands to the preset below, alone or inside a list. |
| `tags` | `list[str]` | `["TODO"]` | `["TODO", "FIXME", "HACK", "XXX"]` | Tags to look for. Tags are matched on word boundaries, longest first. |
| `ignore_case` | `bool` | `false` | same | Whether to match tags case insensitively. |
| `exclude_dirs` | `dict[str, list[str]]` | `built-in list` | same | Directories to skip, with the same shape as `BaseConfig.exclude_dirs`. Added to the built-in exclusions, never replacing them. A table, see below. |
| `exclude_files` | `dict[str, list[str]]` | `built-in list` | same | Files to skip, with the same shape as `BaseConfig.exclude_files`. Added to the built-in exclusions, never replacing them. A table, see below. |
| `require_comment` | `bool` | `false` | `true` | Whether a tag must be inside a comment to count. Which files have which comment syntax is defined in `todonotifier.languages`; files of unknown types are matched anywhere. |
| `use_git_blame` | `bool` | `false` | `true` | Whether to fill missing authors and dates from git blame. |
| `default_due_days` | `Optional[int]` | `unset` | `90` | Days after the creation date (from git blame, so it needs `use_git_blame`) at which an undated TODO becomes stale. None or 0 disables default due dates. `0` turns default due dates off (TOML has no null). The maximum is 36500. |
| `respect_gitignore` | `bool` | `false` | `true` | Whether to skip files ignored by git (`.gitignore`), inside a git repository. |
| `repo_web_url` | `Optional[str]` | `unset` | same | Web URL of the repository (e.g. https://github.com/org/repo), used with `commit_sha` to build deep links. Defaults to None, in which case it is detected from the environment or the `origin` remote when `use_git_blame` is on. |
| `commit_sha` | `Optional[str]` | `unset` | same | Commit the scanned tree corresponds to, used with `repo_web_url` to build deep links. Defaults to None, in which case it is detected (`GITHUB_SHA` or `HEAD`) when `use_git_blame` is on. |

### Exclusions

`exclude_dirs` and `exclude_files` are tables with these optional lists, all added to the built-in exclusions (case is ignored):

| Entry | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | Exact file or directory names, for example `vendor`. |
| `pattern` | Regular expressions that must match the whole name, for example `.*_cache`. |
| `abs_path` | Absolute paths. |

The built-in directory names are `__pycache__`, `.git`, `.env`, `.venv`, `env`, `venv`, `ENV`, `env.bak`, `venv.bak`, `.history`, `.local`, `.vscode`, `build`, `develop-eggs`, `dist`, `downloads`, `lib64`, `parts`, `sdist`, `var`, `wheels`, `pip-wheel-metadata`, `share/python-wheels`, `htmlcov`, `.tox`, `.nox`, `.hypothesis`, `.pytest_cache`, `instance`, `_build`, `target`, `profile_default`, `__pypackages__`, `site`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pyre`, `migrations`.

The built-in file names are `.coverage`, `pip-log.txt`, `pip-delete-this-directory.txt`, `local_settings.py`, `db.sqlite3`, `db.sqlite3-journal`, `.webassets-cache`, `.scrapy`, `.ipynb_checkpoints`, `ipython_config.py`, `.python-version`, `celerybeat-schedule`, `celerybeat.pid`, `.spyderproject`, `.spyproject`, `.ropeproject`, `.dmypy.json`, `dmypy.json`, `nosetests.xml`, `coverage.xml`.

## The `common` extensions

`extensions = "common"` expands to: `py`, `js`, `jsx`, `ts`, `tsx`, `java`, `kt`, `go`, `rs`, `rb`, `php`, `c`, `h`, `cpp`, `hpp`, `cs`, `swift`, `scala`, `sh`, `sql`, `yaml`, `yml`, `toml`, `html`, `css`, `scss`, `md`.

## `fail_on`

When the command line exits with 1. The default is `none`, and `--fail-on` beats the file. It does not change which TODOs are found.

| Value | Fails when |
|---|---|
| `none` | Never fail because of the TODOs found (the default). |
| `expired` | Fail if a TODO has an explicit `{date}` that has passed (overdue). |
| `stale` | Fail on overdue TODOs and on stale ones (a default due date has passed). |
| `any` | Fail if there is any TODO at all. |
| `incomplete` | Fail if a TODO has no owner written in the comment (`@user` or `TAG(user)`) or no explicit `{date}`. A `git blame` author and a default due date do not count. |

## `[authors]`

Maps git author emails to the handle shown in reports, for example `"ashu@example.com" = "ashu"`. Emails are matched in lower case. It fills `ScanSettings.author_aliases`.

## `[notify.NAME]`

Notifiers for `todonotifier notify` (see [Notifications](../notifications.md)). A config file never holds secrets: every key ending in `_env` is the **name** of an environment variable, and a key such as `webhook`, `url`, `password` or `token` is rejected. Every table also accepts `enabled` (boolean, default `true`). `NAME` is one of: `slack`, `teams`, `webhook`, `email`.

### `[notify.slack]`

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `webhook_env` | string (variable name) | yes | Name of the environment variable that holds the Slack incoming webhook URL. |
| `max_items` | integer, at least 1 | no | Most TODOs shown in each section of the message (default 10). |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Set to `false` to keep the table but skip the notifier. |

### `[notify.teams]`

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `webhook_env` | string (variable name) | yes | Name of the environment variable that holds the Microsoft Teams (Workflows) webhook URL. |
| `max_items` | integer, at least 1 | no | Most TODOs shown in each section of the message (default 10). |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Set to `false` to keep the table but skip the notifier. |

### `[notify.webhook]`

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url_env` | string (variable name) | yes | Name of the environment variable that holds the URL that receives the JSON. |
| `headers_env` | string (variable name) | no | Name of an environment variable that holds a JSON object of extra headers, for example `{"Authorization": "Bearer ..."}`. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Set to `false` to keep the table but skip the notifier. |

### `[notify.email]`

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `smtp_host` | string | yes | SMTP server host name. |
| `smtp_port` | integer, 1 to 65535 | no | SMTP port. Default: 587 with `starttls = true`, else 465 (SSL). |
| `sender` | string | yes | Address the email is sent from. |
| `recipients` | list of strings | yes | Addresses the email is sent to. |
| `username_env` | string (variable name) | no | Name of the environment variable that holds the SMTP login, if it is not the sender. |
| `password_env` | string (variable name) | yes | Name of the environment variable that holds the SMTP password. |
| `starttls` | boolean | no | Connect on a plain port and upgrade with STARTTLS (default false). |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Set to `false` to keep the table but skip the notifier. |
